questions.prompt: What distinguishes computational reproduction from replication here?
questions.answer: Reproduction uses the same data and analysis; replication examines the question with new data.

questions.prompt: Does one failed replication conclusively disprove a result?
questions.answer: No; compare uncertainty, methods, contexts and potential errors.
questions.feedback: List two reasons estimates may differ.

questions.prompt: Why document deviations from a protocol?
questions.answer: So readers can assess how departures may affect interpretation and distinguish planned from exploratory analysis.
questions.feedback: Give an example of a meaningful deviation.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Produces a usable repeatability packet and interprets agreement or discrepancy without overclaiming.
scoring.transfer: Exchange a synthetic-data protocol with another learner or simulate a second study yourself. Record deviations and explain how a different estimate should change your confidence, without claiming definitive proof or disproof.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
